ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)

clock_waveform.SWCLK_role: Serial Wire Clock. Generated by the debug host. Free-running during a transaction; may be stopped between transactions.
clock_waveform.rising_edge: Target samples SWDIO during Request and Data-Write phases.
clock_waveform.falling_edge: Target drives SWDIO during ACK and Data-Read phases.
clock_waveform.frequency_range: Typical 1-50 MHz; some probes go to 100 MHz. Implementation-defined per target.

reset_waveform.line_reset_sequence: SWDIO held HIGH for ≥ 50 consecutive SWCLK rising edges forces SW-DP Idle.
reset_waveform.selection_sequence_swd_to_jtag: 16-bit pattern 0xE73C (LSB first on SWDIO) preceded and followed by ≥ 50 cycles SWDIO=HIGH.
reset_waveform.selection_sequence_jtag_to_swd: 16-bit pattern 0xE79E (LSB first on TMS) preceded and followed by ≥ 50 cycles TMS=HIGH.

rows: SWDIO target drive delay (from SWCLK falling)
timing_parameters_per_device.notes: ADIv5 does not specify absolute values; per-device datasheets do.

clock_and_reset_waveform_ahb.HCLK: Single rising-edge clock per AHB interface.
clock_and_reset_waveform_ahb.HRESETn: Active LOW; the only active-LOW signal in AHB.

clock_and_reset_waveform_apb.PCLK: Rising edge times all APB transfers.
clock_and_reset_waveform_apb.PRESETn: Active LOW; normally tied to system bus reset.

sequence: T0: Manager drives HADDR=A, HWRITE=0; HREADY=1.
T1: Subordinate samples address+control on rising HCLK.
T2: Subordinate drives HRDATA=Data(A); Manager samples on T3.
Address phase of next transfer overlaps data phase.

ahb_waited_transfer_waveform.case: Read transfer with two wait states (Figure 3-3)
sequence: One-cycle address phase.
Data phase extended over three cycles: HREADY=0, 0, then 1 with HRDATA=Data(A).
Address phase of next transfer also extended.
Cycle 1: HRESP=1, HREADYOUT=0.
Cycle 2: HRESP=1, HREADYOUT=1.
Manager option: continue burst OR drive HTRANS=IDLE during the 2-cycle ERROR to cancel.
T0-T1: NONSEQ at 0x20.
T1-T2: BUSY at 0x24.
T2-T3: SEQ at 0x24 (Manager continues).
T3-T4: SEQ at 0x28.
T4-T5: SEQ at 0x2C with wait state (HREADY=0).
T5-T6: data of 0x28 returns.
Cycle 1: NONSEQ read, HMASTLOCK=1, HADDR=A.
Cycle 2: NONSEQ write, HMASTLOCK=1, HADDR=A.
Cycle 3: IDLE, HMASTLOCK=0.
T0-T1: IDLE (PSEL=0, PENABLE=0).
T1: PADDR=Addr1, PWRITE=1, PSEL=1, PWDATA=Data1 — SETUP.
T2: PENABLE=1, PREADY=1 — ACCESS; transfer completes.
T3: bus may go IDLE or directly to next SETUP.
SETUP at T1.
ACCESS at T2 with PREADY=0.
ACCESS at T3 with PREADY=0.
ACCESS at T4 with PREADY=1 — transfer completes.
SETUP at T1, ACCESS at T2 with PREADY=0.
ACCESS at T3 with PREADY=1 and PSLVERR=1 — error signaled.
After T3: bus returns to IDLE.

edges: SETUP -> ACCESS unconditional next rising PCLK
ACCESS -> IDLE on PREADY=1 + no further transfer
ACCESS -> SETUP on PREADY=1 + back-to-back transfer

max_outstanding_rules.ahb: AHB-Lite is single-Manager; only one outstanding transfer at a time (no AXI-style outstanding queues). Pipelining means address phase of next transfer overlaps data phase of current transfer.
max_outstanding_rules.apb: APB has no pipelining; only one transfer in flight at a time; minimum 2 PCLK cycles per transfer.

interconnect_combination_rules.ahb_HREADY_chain: Multiplexor combines all Subordinate HREADYOUTs into a single global HREADY broadcast (Figure 4-2). HRDATA / HRESP / HEXOKAY mux'd by decoder HSEL.
interconnect_combination_rules.ahb_apb_bridge: AHB-to-APB bridge is an AHB Subordinate + APB Manager; PSLVERR -> HRESP=ERROR.

swdio_waveform.SWDIO_role: Bidirectional serial data. Host-driven during Request and Data-Write; target-driven during ACK and Data-Read.
swdio_waveform.park_bit_behavior: Bit 7 of Request (Park=1) drives SWDIO HIGH before the host releases the line.

transaction_waveform_summary: Host drives SWDIO from idle (HIGH) and begins the Request: bits 0..7 LSB-first on SWCLK rising edges.
Park=1 leaves SWDIO HIGH; host tri-states; Turnaround A (1 SWCLK cycle by default).
Target drives the 3-bit ACK on the falling edges of the next 3 SWCLKs.
If ACK=OK: for a Read, target drives the next 32 SWDIO cycles with the data LSB-first.
If ACK=OK: for a Write, host drives the next 32 SWDIO cycles with the data LSB-first.
If ACK=WAIT or FAULT: host treats the next 32+1 bits as junk and either retries (WAIT) or reads CTRL/STAT + ABORT (FAULT).
posted_read_waveform_summary: Host issues Read of AP register N: ACK=OK; data is actually the result of the previous AP read.
Host issues second Read: data is the actual result of read N.
To recover the last read, host reads DP.RDBUFF (APnDP=0, A[3:2]=0xC, RnW=1).
